Hey - I've reviewed your changes and they look great!

### Sourcery assessment

**Needs a human reviewer.** A failed stream read now finalizes and exports a span marked with the error; if that behavior is wrong, the emitted telemetry remains after a revert, though it is bounded and can be handled as bad observability data. No application data or access decisions are changed.

## Reviewer's Guide Updates the Mistral and Groq sync/async stream wrappers to finalize and mark spans as failed when iteration raises—including connection errors and cancellation—while preserving exactly-once cleanup; adds regression tests confirming one exported ERROR span when callers do not close or context-manage the stream. #### Sequence diagram for failed Mistral and Groq stream iteration ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant StreamWrapper participant UnderlyingStream participant Span participant Exporter Caller->>StreamWrapper: __next__() / __anext__() StreamWrapper->>UnderlyingStream: __next__() / __anext__() UnderlyingStream-->>StreamWrapper: chunk Caller->>StreamWrapper: __next__() / __anext__() StreamWrapper->>UnderlyingStream: __next__() / __anext__() UnderlyingStream--xStreamWrapper: BaseException StreamWrapper->>StreamWrapper: _finalize_streaming_span(error) StreamWrapper->>Span: handle_exception(error) StreamWrapper->>Span: process_streaming_chat_response() Span->>Exporter: export ERROR span StreamWrapper-->>Caller: re-raise error ``` #### State diagram for streaming span lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Streaming Streaming --> Streaming: __next__() / __anext__() returns chunk Streaming --> FinalizedOK: StopIteration / StopAsyncIteration Streaming --> FinalizedError: read raises BaseException FinalizedError --> FinalizedError: repeated close or context exit FinalizedOK --> FinalizedOK: repeated close or context exit FinalizedOK --> [*] FinalizedError --> [*] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Finalize streaming spans when iteration fails, preserving the failure status and error details. |
  • Catch any BaseException from sync and async reads, finalize the span with the error, and re-raise it.
  • Track whether streaming failed and prevent normal response processing from overwriting ERROR with OK.
  • Retain exactly-once finalization and avoid duplicate exception handling during later close or context-manager cleanup.

  • Assert that each scenario exports exactly one ERROR span without explicit close or context-manager usage.

Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai/dashboard/review-settings?connection=github&owner=openlit&from_surface=github_bot&intent=review_settings) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).
